newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said Commissioner Hans van den Broek and Bulgarian Prime Minister Ivan Kostov and Foreign Affairs Minister Kadeshda Mihailova would be available to reporters for pictures and questions in the VIP corner at 1430/1230 GMT.

Van der Pas said Commissioner Padraig Flynn would hold a news conference on workers information and consultation on Wednesday at 1215/1015 GMT. He said Commission President Jacques Santer and Commissioner Mario Monti would follow with a news conference on the internal market action plan at 1230/1030 GMT.
Van der Pas said Santer would present the Commission opinions for the Amsterdam European Council at the European Parliament plenary session on June 11 and that he would brief reporters afterwoods.

Spokesman Willy Helin said that German construction group Hochtief AG and Deutsche Bank AG had announced on Monday that they were giving up their plans to take a stake in construction firm Philipp Holzmann AG. Helin said there was a high risk that the Commission would have rejected the deal if a decision had to be given.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/465: Commissioner Pinheiro welcomes Council's resolution on conflict prevention in Africa.
- IP/97/467: State of health of women in the European Union.
- IP/97/470: Padraig Flynn welcomes the establishment of the European Monitoring Centre for Racism and Xenophobia.
- IP/97/472: Bangladesh: the Commission approves emergency humanitarian aid worth ECU 350,000 for victims of "One Bravo" cyclone.
- IP/97/474: International energy cooperation through the SYNERGY Programme - review of activities 1994-1996.
- IP/97/475: The Commission supports industrial restructuring in 12 French regions.
- Speech/97/128: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer at European Unions Confederation.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Economy and Finance No 1997-17: Quarterly national accounts - Fourth quarter 1996.
